text: Welcome to your post-operative evaluation. You mentioned occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty; can you describe the exact location and quality of that pain, and how long it has been occurring?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The pain occurring while eating and the discomfort with earrings suggest possible tragus pain or involvement of the auriculotemporal nerve; could you explain if the pain also radiates to your jaw or temple, and have you noticed any discharge or fluid leakage from the right ear canal recently?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Auriculotemporal Neuralgia (triggered by V3 nerve irritation post-tympanoplasty).

The normal otoscopy and tympanometry effectively rule out graft failure or active infection; your shooting pain upon eating (jaw movement) and tragus tenderness are classic signs of nerve irritation in the distribution of the auriculotemporal nerve.
